description: User story under REQ-189 for the review stamp (FBS-213). The hash is sha256 over the canonical record without review plus the sorted (path, sha256) pairs of every wireframe file; the verb refuses on any structural failure; discovery:reviewed compares the stamped hash with the hash recomputed now; the managed agent-instructions block says the harness never runs the verb on its own.
asA: a product owner signing off DISCOVERY
iWant: to review the journey the tool shows me and stamp it, and to have that stamp go stale the moment a journey or a wireframe changes
soThat: "reviewed" is a fact the tool can check, not a sentence in a plan

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a journey that passes every structural check, when the journey review verb runs with --by and a name, then ReviewStamp.state equals "reviewed", ReviewStamp.by equals the name, ReviewStamp.at carries the time and the discoveryHash of the record, and ReviewStamp.wireframeHashes carries one sha256 per screen with a wireframe.

[happy] Given a reviewed record, when discovery:reviewed evaluates with the record and every wireframe file unchanged, then it passes, and the review verb that produced the stamp printed the one-line summary (journeys, steps, screens, interruptions mapped) before writing.
[failure] Given a journey that fails any structural check, when the journey review verb runs, then it exits 4 printing the failing checks and writes no ReviewStamp.

[edge] Given a reviewed record, when a wireframe file's bytes change or a journey source is re-minted, then discovery:reviewed fails as stale with a why naming the changed screens or journey, and a second review at the new hash makes it pass again.

[must-not] Given the managed agent-instructions block, when rcf init or rcf doctor --fix writes it, then it carries the rule that the harness never runs the journey review verb on its own beside the ADR-4132 prototype rule, and no verb other than journey review ever writes ReviewStamp.

title: the product owner reviews the journey and the review is sealed by a content hash
